g.text: DNSSEC chain of trust for example.com
✓ DNSSEC is on and validates for example.com
Every link from the root down to example.com is signed and checks out: each parent
vouches for its child's key with a DS record, and each zone signs its records with that
key. DNSSEC protects against forged DNS answers: someone on the network, or a poisoned
resolver cache, can't send visitors to a fake address without the signature check
failing. It doesn't encrypt DNS or hide which sites you visit. Validating resolvers
Nothing to do. When you change DNS host or keys, update the DS record at the
registrar at the same time, or validation breaks.
